subject: MAP: Multi-region benchmarks + close timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@vertica.ai>, Timothy Keller <timothy.keller@globex.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Multi-region benchmarks + close timeline

Hi Elaine / Tim,

Per our MAP review, we want to lock the performance acceptance criteria and the final close timeline this sprint. Attached is an outline of the evaluation plan we discussed on the call (scope: latency, throughput, TTFT, concurrency, and multi-region routing/failover). High-level asks:

- We will run synchronized tests across US (us-west-2), EU (eu-west-1), and APAC (ap-southeast-1).
- Target workload: 128-token prompts, 50–500 concurrent sessions, and peak bursts to 1k concurrent for short windows.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), TTFT (first token from server), sustained tokens/sec per model variant, and failover routing hit-rate for simulated region outage.
- Acceptance thresholds to meet for the MAP: p95 < 350ms (us), < 420ms (eu), < 520ms (apac); TTFT < 120ms across regions for warmed KV cache; sustained throughput > 150k tokens/sec per 8xA100 equivalent for the primary model.

Can your team run the coordinated test window next Tuesday afternoon (Feb 10) and share the raw measurements + a short summary PDF? If results look good we can proceed with the proposed close timeline: legal review by Feb 18, PO by Feb 24, and go-live pilot week of Mar 2.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Jonas —

Thanks, we'll run the coordinated windows on Feb 10 as suggested. Our ops/QA team will execute three 45-minute windows (US/EU/APAC) plus a 15-minute simulated failover in the middle of each window. Deliverables: raw traces, per-region summary CSVs, and a one-page top-line PDF.

Couple clarifying points:
- Which model variant should we use? You mentioned a quantized 8-bit baseline and an fp16 variant for latency comparison.
- Do you want us to include client-side RTT (to emulate real-world) or only server-side server processing times?

Proposed: run both model variants; collect server-side timings and optional client RTT so we can separate network vs. inference latency.

I'll loop in ops: ops+qa@acme-corp.com will coordinate load generation from our side.

—Elaine
Elaine Park, Sr. Solutions Engineer
Vertica AI

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM Elaine Park <elaine@vertica.ai> wrote:
> Jonas —
>
> Thanks, we'll run the coordinated windows on Feb 10 as suggested. Our ops/QA team will execute three 45-minute windows (US/EU/APAC) plus a 15-minute simulated failover in the middle of each window.

Thanks Elaine — Marcus and I collected the consolidated numbers and attached the PDF summary. Top-line results below (server-side measurements, warmed cache where noted):

US (us-west-2) — quantized-8b: p50=68ms, p95=210ms, p99=410ms; TTFT median=95ms (warmed); sustained throughput=162k tokens/sec per 8xA100 baseline; concurrency linear up to 520 sessions, degraded gracefully beyond 700 with shedding policy.
EU (eu-west-1) — quantized-8b: p50=82ms, p95=295ms, p99=540ms; TTFT median=112ms; sustained throughput=148k tokens/sec; observed slight jitter at high concurrency due to cross-AZ routing.
APAC (ap-southeast-1) — quantized-8b: p50=150ms, p95=410ms, p99=780ms; TTFT median=165ms; sustained throughput=132k tokens/sec; cold start penalties for some nodes during burst tests.

FP16 variant improved p50/p95 by ~10–15% on average but increased cost by ~1.4x—details in attached PDF (redwood-benchmark-report-20260210.pdf). Failover test (simulate eu region loss): multi-region routing switched to fallback in <6 seconds on average; routing hit-rate (successful failover traffic) = 97.8% after configuration tweaks (local DNS TTL + fast health probes).

Notes / recommended MAP acceptance adjustments:
- Relax APAC p95 threshold to 450ms given realistic network RTTs; require improvement plan to push p95 < 420ms within 30 days.
- Accept FP16 as optional for premium tier customers; default ship with quantized 8b for cost predictability.
- Add a 95% routing failover success requirement to the MAP (we measured 97.8% today).

Next steps: Elaine / Globex — confirm these numbers look reasonable. If accepted we'll update the MAP spreadsheet (MAP-v3-closure-plan.xlsx) and target legal/PO dates in the original email.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the thoroughness. A few quick questions from our infra team after reviewing the PDF:

1) For the failover test, can you confirm whether client-side connection pooling was preserved after the route switch or if new connections were required? That affects our session affinity assumptions.
2) The APAC cold-starts: are those specific to the instance profile used, or expected across any on-demand scaling?

If those are clarifications we can accept the recommended APAC p95 relaxation for the MAP. We'll approve updating the MAP spreadsheet as long as we have a 30-day remediation plan for APAC.

—Tim

Globex Industries

Tim — thanks for the quick review and thoughtful questions. Quick answers and MAP update: 

1) Connection handling on failover: our routing approach preserves long-lived TLS connections where possible via in-region TCP handoff and a short-lived proxy layer; however some clients will reopen sockets depending on their NAT/idle-time. In our tests ~62% of pooled connections persisted, the rest negotiated new handshakes — included in the report's connection table. We'll add an explicit note in the MAP to call out session-affinity expectations and recommended client timeouts.

2) APAC cold-starts: primarily tied to scale-out from zero for some autoscaling groups in the APAC fleet profile we used. A warmed pool removes the majority of spikes; as part of the MAP remediation plan we will provide a warm standby strategy and pre-warming policy to Globex within 7 business days.

Updated MAP items and dates (ref MAP-v3-closure-plan.xlsx):
- Accept thresholds: US p95 < 350ms, EU p95 < 420ms, APAC p95 < 450ms (remediation plan due Feb 23).
- Failover acceptance: >=95% successful failover routing and mean switchover <10s.
- Legal review: Feb 18; PO target: Feb 24; Go-live pilot: week of Mar 2.

If these look good I'll mark the MAP as "accepted pending PO" and ask legal to kick off the SOW redline. Thanks everyone — close timeline remains on track assuming PO by Feb 24.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions
